general: Extract every entity of the supplied types. Return exact spans from the query. Leave other text unlabelled.

classes.name: Review
classes.description: Refers to an evaluation or assessment of a movie's quality, performance, or other aspects.
rules: RE1 It includes expressions or phrases that indicate personal opinions, critiques, or judgments about a movie's overall merit, such as greatest, excellent, disappointing, and similar evaluative terms.
RE2 It also includes expressions such as five stars rated, lowest rated or recommended, which provide an indication of the reviewer's assessment of the movie.
RE3 Examples: "good", "best", "must see", "classic", "funniest".

classes.name: Rating
classes.description: Refers to the official classification or content rating assigned to a movie by a recognized film rating organization.
rules: RA1 Ratings provide guidance to audiences and parents about the movie's suitability based on its content, themes, and age-appropriateness.
RA2 Ratings can include various classifications such as MPAA (Motion Picture Association) ratings like R-Rated, PG-13, PG, or other regional and international rating systems.
RA3 A Rating span is only the code, without "rated" or "rating": "r" in "r rated", "g" in "g rated", "pg 13" in "a pg 13 rating". "unrated" is also a Rating.
RA4 Examples: "r", "pg 13", "pg", "g", "nc 17".

classes.name: Director
classes.description: Refers to an individual who is responsible for overseeing and guiding the artistic vision and creative elements of a movie.
rules: DI1 The director plays a pivotal role in shaping the film's narrative, performances, and overall execution.
DI2 The Director entity includes the names of both film directors and television directors, as long as they are relevant to the movie context.
DI3 Examples: "steven spielberg", "james cameron", "directed", "clint eastwood", "alfred hitchcock".

classes.name: Song
classes.description: Refers to a musical composition or piece of music that is associated with a movie.
rules: SO1 This includes individual songs featured in the movie's soundtrack, as well as musical groups and singers who perform those songs.
SO2 The Song entity class encompasses both original songs created specifically for the movie and pre-existing songs used in the movie's soundtrack.
SO3 Song is a song title or a soundtrack mention: "suicide is painless", "i will always love you", "soundtracks"; praise words such as ok, good or mediocre are never Song.
SO4 Examples: "soundtrack", "my heart will go on", "theme song", "i will always love you", "john williams".

classes.name: Tittle
classes.description: Refers to the name or label that uniquely identifies a specific movie or film production.
rules: TI1 It includes the official title of the movie, which is used for identification, promotion, and reference purposes.
TI2 The Title entity class encompasses the full names of movies, as well as any abbreviations or alternative titles that are commonly associated with the movie.
TI3 Keep the whole movie name, with its leading "the": "the goonies", "the shining", "the hunger games", "shrek the third", "robin hood men in tights".
TI4 A movie named after a person or hero is Tittle, not Character, when the query is about that movie: "austin powers", "thelma and louise", "shrink".
TI5 A movie name asked about is Tittle, not Rating, also in a question about its rating: "doom", "if you were me", "white men cant jump".
TI6 Examples: "inception", "the shining", "wall e", "star wars", "titanic".

classes.name: RatingsAverage
classes.description: Refers to the collective or average assessment of a movie's quality, popularity, or critical acclaim based on reviews, ratings, or awards from various sources.
rules: RAT1 This entity includes general descriptions of the overall reception of the movie, such as 3-star rating, award-winning, critically heralded, box office hit, or similar expressions that provide an indication of the movie's reception.

RAT2 How much viewers liked the movie is RatingsAverage, not Review or Rating: "really good", "really popular", "very popular", "very good", "was liked a lot", "liked by many", "two thumbs up", "ok", "mediocre", "decent".
RAT3 Keep the words rated and ratings inside these spans: "highly rated", "well rated", "rated well", "highest rated", "excellent ratings".
RAT4 Praise words right next to a rating code are still RatingsAverage, not Rating: "ok", "mediocre", "really good".
RAT5 A score is RatingsAverage, never Rating: label just the number, with stars when it follows: "six", "seven", "eight", "nine stars"; never label the word average or rating alone.
RAT6 Examples: "average", "ok", "mediocre", "highly rated", "critically acclaimed".

classes.name: Year
classes.description: Refers to a numerical representation of the calendar year in which a specific movie was released or produced.
rules: YE1 The Year entity class encompasses four-digit numerical values that indicate the specific year of a movie's release or production.
YE2 Relative periods are Year, without "the": "last ten years", "past four years", "this year", "last decade".

classes.name: Genre
classes.description: Refers to a category or classification that characterizes the style, theme, or tone of a movie.
rules: GE1 Genres are used to identify and categorize movies based on their common characteristics and storytelling elements.
GE2 Genres can be broad categories (e.g., Action, Comedy, Drama) or more specific sub-genres.
GE3 Film kinds are Genre also when used as a noun: "documentary", "musical", "mockumentary", "animation", "animated", "biography", "war", "family".
GE4 Examples: "action", "comedy", "horror", "fantasy", "science fiction".

classes.name: Plot
classes.description: A plot element or theme is a recurring concept, event, or motif that plays a significant role in the development of a story, narrative, or work of fiction.
rules: PL1 For example what happens in a movie (murder, love at first sight, cars that fly, horse racing), the type of characters in the movie (vampires, zombies, fugitives, cats), where the movie was recorded (British, American), among others.
PL2 What the movie is about is Plot: the subject after "about", without "a" or "an": "dog", "prisoner", "redemption", "attempted suicide".

PL3 Topics, settings and kinds of characters are Plot, not Genre or Tittle, also right before "movie": "zombie", "superhero", "robot", "finance", "activism", "mad scientist", "samurai", "insanity", "world series".
PL4 Examples: "murder", "vampires", "ghosts", "levitation", "love at first sight".

classes.name: Actor
classes.description: Refers to an individual who plays a role in a movie, including main cast members, supporting actors, and cameo appearances.
rules: AC1 If an individual is known for their work in television, theater, or other media but also appears in movies, they can be considered an Actor in this context.

AC2 A real performer named in the query is Actor, not Character, also right before a genre word: "charlie sheen", "helen hunt", "tom selleck", "edward norton", "halle berry". Character is a role inside the story, such as "james bond" or "snape".
AC3 Singers and bands named in the query are Actor too: "rolling stones", "eilera".
AC4 Examples: "johnny depp", "brad pitt", "tom hanks", "tom cruise", "clint eastwood".

classes.name: Character
classes.description: Refers to a fictional or real individual portrayed in a movie's narrative or storyline.
rules: CH1 It includes main characters, supporting characters, antagonists, and any other roles that contribute to the plot or development of the movie.
CH2 Characters can be human or non-human, and they represent the individuals with specific roles and identities within the movie's fictional universe.
CH3 Examples: "james bond", "indiana jones", "jason bourne", "harry potter", "batman".

classes.name: Trailer
classes.description: Refers to a short promotional video or preview of a movie that is designed to generate interest and excitement among the audience before the movie's release.
rules: TR1 This entity also includes mentions to trailers, such as 'trailer','preview', 'teaser' or 'highlights'.
TR2 Examples: "trailer", "preview", "trailers", "shortest trailer", "star wars".
